findings.body:
Gain 2, Work 2, Harm 4
Raise: Security. Case: normal use - A Windows user copies a suggested command containing a repository-controlled workflow name. The new quoting escapes only ASCII apostrophes, but PowerShell also treats `’` as a single-quote delimiter. For `full_suite_workflow = "nightly’;calc;#.yml"`, `src/forge/fullrun.py:17` prints `gh workflow run 'nightly’;calc;#.yml' --ref main`: the curly quote ends the string, `calc` runs, and the comment hides the suffix. The configuration check at `src/forge/repo.py:929` accepts this value, and the same helper handles worker notes and review reasons. This leaves the earlier command-injection finding open; [PowerShell's quoting rules](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/microsoft.powershell.core/about/about_quoting_rules?view=powershell-7) document the additional delimiters.
(floor: Security)
Adds work: protect shell-sensitive Windows arguments; F 1 x H 3 = 3; 2 x C = 4.

findings.body:
Gain 2, Work 1, Harm 1
Raise: Not done. Case: normal use - A repository names its scheduled workflow `nightly@2am.yml`. Adding `+` fixes the previous example, but the character class still excludes `@`, so Windows prints `'nightly@2am.yml'` while POSIX prints `nightly@2am.yml`. The at-sign inside this argument is literal in [PowerShell](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/microsoft.powershell.core/about/about_parsing?view=powershell-7), and [Python's POSIX quoting](https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/3.11/Lib/shlex.py) leaves it unquoted. The incomplete safe-character set therefore still causes the mismatch identified in the previous finding.
